question: Should OpenClaw accept static `sandbox.docker.env` SecretRefs when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but the durable decision is whether SecretRef-backed credentials are acceptable on a Docker env surface with documented metadata exposure.

options.title: Accept with explicit boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR after maintainer/security review confirms that the existing Docker metadata exposure warning is sufficient for this static config-time SecretRef surface.

options.title: Require stronger warnings first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to make SecretRef-backed Docker env exposure more explicit in docs and audit/configure output before merge.

options.title: Reject env delivery
options.body: Close or pause the linked PR and design a non-env secret delivery mechanism if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after maintainer/security review confirms that the existing Docker metadata exposure warning is sufficient for this static config-time SecretRef surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest recent history across both Docker sandbox env propagation and SecretRef runtime behavior.
